properties.description: The nudge's counting AND its own promise are both trustworthy (tools/test_loop_nudge.py) — 47 cases, 11 new in BL-163 on top of the 8 across BL-161 and BL-111. BL-163 · PRECEDENCE, NOT PRESENCE: a session that edits code, records a ChangeEvent and never calls propagate_change is nudged — the defect was that the impact-check shape keyed on `changes == 0`, firing only when a session recorded NOTHING, so writing the ChangeEvents up AFTER the edits satisfied the very trigger meant to catch writing them up after the edits. ROOT CAUSE IN ONE LINE: `CHANGE_OPS` held `record_change` and `add_change_event`, both RECORDING ops, and no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all — the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. THE COUNTERWEIGHT THE ROW DEMANDED AND THE CASE PINNED FIRST: a session that propagated gets NOTHING, and `propagate_from` counts as looking too, because the impact-check skill sends a speculative "what would this touch?" straight to it. THE CONJUNCTION IS THE GUARD, all three clauses load-bearing and each with its own test: `edits > 0` (a pure design session has no blast radius to compute), `changes > 0` (what keeps this from becoming a second, thresholdless bypass nudge), `propagates == 0`. BL-161'S PRECEDENT HELD: "you never propagated" is a NEGATIVE claim, so a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one drops it, exactly as "the graph was never consulted" does. BL-161 · STATE INTEGRITY: a 60-hook CONCURRENT burst against a seeded tally lands every increment and wipes no sticky field; against the pre-fix script the same burst returned touched=false, artifacts=0 and 6 of 60 edits, because a non-atomic write plus an error-swallowing read let one hook store zeros over the session's record. COUNTERWEIGHT: a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one keeps counting — an existing case required that and was right — but can no longer support the hook's negative claims, because the calls that would refute them are exactly what was lost; and the POSITIVE claim, "N writes went unchecked", still fires after a restart, so the flag is not an off switch. BULK FORMS: set_artifact_checksums, create_nodes and gaps_to_prompts tally as the singular forms they replace. BL-111 · FIRES ONCE: a second stop CYCLE does not nudge again (the promise is per SESSION, and it rested on the harness's stop_hook_active, which is per cycle and never persisted), all THREE blocking branches keep it, and TWO CONCURRENT HOOK PROCESSES on the same Stop produce exactly ONE message — which is the case it was filed from and is not exotic, since reflow2 installs machine-wide AND a project may carry its own registration and the two command spellings do not dedupe. COUNTERWEIGHT: the claim is spent by NUDGING, not by STOPPING, so a session with nothing owed stops silently and keeps its one nudge.
properties.findings: THE WRITE NUDGE STILL TAKES PRECEDENCE and that test is not vacuous — disabling the write branch fails it. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: never count propagation (6 failures, both counterweights); drop `changes > 0` (7 failures, including BL-90's ENTIRE bypass family — the measurement that proves that clause is what stops this swallowing the older branch); drop `edits > 0` (1); drop `propagate_from` (1); drop the once-only claim (1); remove the branch entirely, i.e. ship the defect (5); and disable the write branch (14, including the precedence case). A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE TESTS FAILING, not by reading: `update_state` re-serialises from an explicit key whitelist — a THIRD hand-kept copy of the state's key set beside `blank_state` and `parse_state` — so the new counter incremented in memory and was silently dropped on every write. That is BL-159's shape a third time, inside one file. THE MUTATION CHECK ONCE CAUGHT MY OWN TEST PASSING FOR FREE: the first concurrency helper looped communicate(), which blocks until each child exits, so the children ran serially and the test stayed green against the UNFIXED script.
properties.name: The nudge's counting and its own promise are both trustworthy
